findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plain text in the instance user_data bootstrap script. These credentials are readable by anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute access and are committed to source control, so they must be treated as compromised and rotated immediately.
The instance does not enable metadata service HTTP tokens (IMDSv2), leaving IMDSv1 unauthenticated metadata access enabled, which permits SSRF to escalate into credential theft.
The EBS volume does not set 'encrypted = true', so the volume is created unencrypted by default, exposing data at rest to anyone with access to the underlying storage.
The EBS snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and no encryption is specified, so the snapshot is unencrypted and exposes data at rest when copied or shared.

The security group allows SSH (port 22) inbound from 0.0.0.0/0, granting the entire internet access to the instance's SSH service, which is a broad attack surface for brute force and unauthorized access.

The security group allows HTTP (port 80) inbound from 0.0.0.0/0. While port 80 web serving may be intended, this combined with the broad egress and public subnet does not constrain access; more importantly this is flagged per CIS against unrestricted ingress of 0.0.0.0/0.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing a data exfiltration path and a channel to command-and-control infrastructure.

The web host instance is placed in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and has an internet gateway and 0.0.0.0/0 route, giving the instance a public IP and internet exposure, increasing attack surface.
The S3 bucket used for VPC flow log storage does not enable default encryption, so flow log data stored at rest is not encrypted.
